remarks.agent_quote: chat (pipeline, 2025-12-30) settles that on a clean work dir with nothing to load, verify_sidecar never fires and the ledger comes back carrying the status it was built with -- i.e. 'created', not 'adopted'/'verified'. My load_ledger verifies unconditionally, and the processor re-derives in-loop with the default 'verified'. I should fix both so the empty/fresh case reports 'created' while a resume against an existing log still adopts/verifies.
remarks.note: Read correctly as written (a truly clean/empty work dir keeps its built status), but the agent's fix (gating on `if not records: return ledger` inside load_ledger, and defaulting `_ledger_from`'s status param to 'created') does not address the actual defect: processor.run()'s per-turn loop calls self._ledger_from(records) after every append with a hardcoded status default, clobbering whatever provenance status load_cache/verify_sidecar had just computed at the top of run() (created/adopted/verified). So a resumed run whose checkpoint was deleted (records non-empty) still gets overwritten to 'created' on the first loop turn instead of keeping the 'adopted' that verify_sidecar correctly set moments earlier. See turn_ledger.py _ledger_from() default status parameter, processor.run() lines around records.append()/self._ledger_from(records).

lost_facts.assertion: judge_r1_observability: eq(o['nockpt_status'], 'adopted', 'no checkpoint -> adopted') — CTRF: "no checkpoint -> adopted: 'created' != 'adopted'" (this is the FIRST failing check in the probe/judge sequence; opening 186-byte write, done 189-byte state, and the stale-checkpoint desync all passed before this point).
lost_facts.evidence: The agent's own module is internally correct at the function level: verify_sidecar(working_dir, ledger) (written ~line 5758 in the transcript / confirmed in the full JSON tool call at msg 183) returns replace(ledger, status='adopted') whenever read_sidecar() is None — i.e. a missing checkpoint against an existing log correctly reads 'adopted'. But processor.run() (full JSON msg 193, 'async def run(...)') never keeps that status once the loop starts: on every appended response it calls `ledger = self._ledger_from(records)` (no status kwarg), and `_ledger_from`'s signature is `def _ledger_from(self, records, status: str = "verified") -> TurnLedger` (originally) then `status: str = "created"` after the agent's own late 'fix' at transcript line 8703-8704 (triggered by remark g7.r1.fix30, '2025-12-30 #pipeline': 'clean work dir, ran it end to end - nothing to load so verify_sidecar never fired, and the ledger came back still carrying the status it was built with'). The agent's fix (`if not records: return ledger` inside load_ledger, plus the _ledger_from default flip to 'created') is scoped to the wrong condition: it keys off whether load_ledger's *own* `records` argument is empty, but load_cache/load_ledger is only ever called ONCE at the very top of run() (line 44: `ledger = self.load_cache(working_dir)`); the correctly-computed 'adopted' status it returns is then immediately overwritten by the loop's `self._ledger_from(records)` calls on every turn (lines 63-64, 84-85 of the run() body), which always stamp the loop-default status regardless of what load_cache/verify_sidecar determined. Before the fix this silently forced every completed run to 'verified'; after the fix it forces every completed run to 'created'. Neither preserves 'adopted' for a resume whose checkpoint file was deleted but whose log already has content — exactly the probe's 'no checkpoint at all' scenario, which runs one more turn through that same loop after `sidecar.unlink()`. The agent's own reasoning (line 8703) correctly diagnosed the truly-fresh-workdir half of the requirement (g7.r1.fix30) but never revisited whether the loop's hardcoded status default also clobbers the adopted/verified provenance for every other run — it treated the fix as complete and moved straight to writing new unit tests for the fresh-run case only (line 8760-8776), never re-testing the 'delete the sidecar mid-log' resume path its own earlier work (l9, l16, l12, rev1) had established.

search_strategy: Very thorough and largely mechanical: the agent enumerated all 12 Mattermost channels via the API (step ~31, transcript line 2671) and bulk-dumped every post in every channel to local files (/tmp/chat/*.txt, ~10k posts) rather than searching piecemeal, then grepped those files repeatedly for targeted terms as its model of the requirement grew (TURN_LEDGER_VERSION, verify_sidecar, is_completed, COMPLETION_SENTINEL, etc.). For the wiki, it used BookStack's /api/search for initial discovery but then, having read in its own onboarding notes (transcript line 143) that BookStack search does not index comments, switched to fetching whole pages by id via /api/pages/{id} (pages 139,143,144,150,152,211,85) so comments came along with the body — this is exactly the discipline the answer key rewards, and it is why all 8 wiki-comment clues plus the 1 wiki-page-body clue in the answer key were found. For mail it used IMAP SEARCH with a keyword list of {ledger, sidecar, sentinel, turn_ledger, next_speaker, seed}, fetched the union of matching message ids in one pass (22 ids), and never re-ran IMAP search with a broader term list — this is the strategy's one real gap: the 'sentinel' search returned 0 hits, and three mail threads (g7.r1.l9, g7.r2.g7r2-l08, g7.r2.g7r2-l05) whose subjects/bodies use different wording ('metadata json isn't on disk', 'stop condition', 'stop sequences') were never fetched at all. Chat coverage was excellent for #code-review, #pipeline, #engineering and #incidents (every clue in those channels the pointer sheet lists was found) but thinner for #cookbooks, #viewer and #releases, where several clues (g7r2-l01, g7r2-l06, say18, say23) were dumped locally but never specifically grepped for. No truncation or crashed helper scripts hurt this run — the one recurring nuisance was a 'terminal output has not changed' watchdog nudging the agent to stop polling on quiet heredoc writes, which did not cost it any content.
end_reason: Not applicable in the 'nothing built' sense — the run completed normally: pushed (provenance.pushed=1), CI green (provenance.ci_green=1), deployed (provenance.deployed=1), suite_ok=1, and 8 of 9 declared facts scored 1. The single 0 is a genuine shipped-code defect (see lost_facts), not an infra or harness failure — the agent's own late self-correction pass (transcript line 8703) is what introduced it, by over-generalizing a legitimate late clue (g7.r1.fix30) into a change that broke a different, already-working code path.
notable: The run's one lost fact was self-inflicted by a *correct* clue: g7.r1.fix30 ('clean work dir keeps created') is real and the agent read it right, but its fix clobbered the adopted-status path for every resumed run because processor.run()'s loop hardcodes _ledger_from's status default on every turn instead of carrying forward what load_cache/verify_sidecar computed once at the top (transcript line 8703-8710, full-JSON msg 299 keystrokes).

Three mail threads were never fetched because the agent's one-shot IMAP keyword list (ledger/sidecar/sentinel/turn_ledger/next_speaker/seed) missed their wording; notably the literal term 'sentinel' returned 0 IMAP hits (transcript line 4313-4314), yet the sentinel-related mail thread g7.r2.g7r2-l11 was still caught under the 'ledger' keyword by coincidence.

All 4 herrings were correctly abandoned in favor of their reversals; two herrings (g7.r1.g7-h2-truncate-is-the-pattern, g7.r2.h2-sentinel-placement-free) were never seen in their original form at all — the agent only ever encountered them paraphrased inside the reversal exchange itself (lines 3626 and 3040/3186), which was still sufficient to avoid following them.

g7.r2.g7r2-l12 (mail-adjacent chat clue giving the exact dataset row content/role) was missed, but this cost nothing: the open ticket's own stated dataset schema (transcript line 109, 'role: the record's name, content: str(response_message)') already supplied that detail, so the hidden clue was redundant with public information for this specific sub-fact.

#cookbooks, #viewer and #releases were dumped in full alongside every other channel but were comparatively under-grepped — 4 of the 14 total misses live there, versus 0 misses in #code-review/#pipeline/#engineering/#incidents, suggesting the agent's search terms tracked the channels it had already found something in rather than sampling every channel evenly.
